source.title: Scaling Laws for Forgetting during Finetuning with Pretraining Data Injection
source.authors: Louis Béthune; D. Grangier; D. Busbridge; Eleonora Gualdoni; Marco Cuturi; Pierre Ablin

record.file_problem: none noted; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study extends scaling-law analysis to pretraining-loss forgetting and target loss during fine-tuning, rather than testing the original pretraining loss laws or compute-optimal allocation directly.
record.gate_note: The study reports fitted scaling laws for fine-tuning and post-fine-tuning pretraining loss, prediction errors, extrapolation errors, and downstream-task evaluations. It does not directly measure loss scaling during pretraining over parameters, tokens, and compute, or search for a compute-optimal parameter/token split. Claims about prior scaling-law work are citations, not results from this study. Detailed iteration traces and figures that do not provide separately stated outcomes are not cataloged.
record.test_reason: The study fits a power law (A/(N^α·Dft^β)+E) to target-domain validation loss after full-parameter fine-tuning. It does this for GPT2-style models from 41M to 1.27B parameters, across 12 Pile domains and OpenHermes instruction fine-tuning, and checks extrapolation to held-out larger settings. This bears on V5 (the fine-tuning regime), V2 (extrapolation) and V7 (data-dependent exponents). The forgetting law models pretraining loss rising after fine-tuning. That is a different construct, so it fits no version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. The authors conclude that fine-tuning loss and pretraining-set forgetting are predictable from model size, available fine-tuning tokens and the injected pretraining fraction, using simple domain-specific scaling laws. They add that injecting even 1% pretraining data mitigates forgetting. They also stress that smaller models forget more, losing up to 95% of pretraining progress.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains GPT2-style models and fits new laws for target-domain fine-tuning loss and post-fine-tuning pretraining loss. It does not reproduce the original pretraining-loss or compute-optimal-allocation measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The fitted coefficients vary by target domain. The reported fit error changes with the selected law form and with whether the pre-fine-tuning loss uses the rewarmed checkpoint; the study also treats the injection fraction as negligible for the target-loss fit.

fits_no_version.finding: Pretraining loss after fine-tuning follows L0pt + A·Dft^β/((1+Bp)N)^α at 0.40% MRE, with domain-dependent α of 0.38–0.81 and β of 0.11–0.60. It extrapolates at 0.73–0.83% MRE. Excluding L0pt or ignoring rewarming worsens the fit.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Forgetting of pretraining loss during fine-tuning grows as a power law in fine-tuning tokens and shrinks with model size and the fraction of pretraining data injected.

fits_no_version.finding: After fine-tuning on Dm mathematics, ARC-easy accuracy degrades. Injecting pretraining data recovers it significantly, by about 4–8 points at larger data sizes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pretraining-data injection mitigates downstream forgetting during fine-tuning.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267, 2025
record.problems: The study restricts base pretraining to the D = 100N isocurve for its main experiments and uses GPT2-style models. Its extrapolation test spans a limited range rather than orders of magnitude. Some downstream outcomes are available only in figures, and the study does not test compute-optimal allocation or architecture variation at fixed parameter count.
record.rows_left_out: The per-domain fine-tuning-law coefficients and per-domain fine-tuning MREs in Table 2 are not listed separately; the aggregate fine-tuning fit is recorded in r1. Figure-only curves and individual iteration traces are omitted where the text does not report a separate numerical outcome. The ARC-easy table's individual model, data-size, and injection-fraction accuracy differences are not expanded into rows; the aggregate textual result and figure are recorded in r22.

untested.parts: All of it. Pretraining loss across N, D and C is not fitted; Table 3 lists L0pt by size only, on a single D=100N isocurve.
Extrapolation over several orders of magnitude, and extrapolation of pretraining loss.
All of it. There is no fixed-compute search for the best parameter/token allocation.
All of it. Shape is not varied at a fixed parameter count.
Other modalities, repeated-data pretraining and transfer. Only full-parameter fine-tuning of text models is tested.
All of it. No downstream accuracy is related to scale or to pretraining loss.
Effects of parameter counting, training schedule and fitting method on the exponents, and curves bending away from a power law.

missing.what: Per-domain fine-tuning-law coefficients: α 0.06–0.19, β 0.01–0.19, E, and MRE 0.35–1.86%. rows_left_out declares these, but the V7 verdict depends on them.
missing.locator: Table 2 (Finetuning Scaling Laws columns); Section 4.5 Analysis

missing.what: Fine-tuning law on checkpoints pretrained on the D=10N isocurve (Freelaw domain) fits with bootstrapped MRE 1.14%.
Authors state the fine-tuning α of 0.12–0.19 is consistent with Hoffmann et al., although Dm math (0.06) and Enron (0.07) fall outside that range.

record.verdict_notes: Not an original source. The forgetting law was the reader's main basis for V5 and V7. I reassigned it to fits_no_version, because it models pretraining loss rising with fine-tuning data rather than loss falling with scale. I removed V6: the downstream evaluations measure the effect of fine-tuning and injection, not scale predictability. The extrapolation range is small (about 4x in parameters, 10x in tokens).

versions.untested_parts: Does not measure held-out pretraining loss as a function of pretraining parameter count, pretraining tokens, or compute while varying the other quantities.
Tests extrapolation for the study's fine-tuning and forgetting laws, not predictions of pretraining loss from the original scaling laws; tested ranges are not orders of magnitude.
No fixed-compute search for a loss-minimizing parameter/token allocation.
Model sizes change multiple architecture dimensions; the study does not compare depth, width, or other architectures at a fixed parameter count.
Tests raw-text fine-tuning and instruction fine-tuning, but not other modalities, repeated pretraining data as a general regime, or transfer beyond the reported fine-tuning settings.
Downstream evaluations are limited to ARC-easy and MMLU on models fine-tuned on Dm mathematics; no downstream scaling law or relation to pretraining loss is fitted.

Shows domain-dependent coefficients and differences among fitted law forms and baseline choices, but does not systematically vary parameter counting, training schedules, or fitting procedures to quantify their effects.
